summary: Build a relevant prospect list, test a clear offer, and find out whether cold email can start useful sales conversations.
author: Bharat Devana
problem: You need a repeatable way to reach the right buyers, without adding more manual prospecting to the team’s day.
hypothesis: Test a focused audience and a small set of messages. Use the replies to learn which buyer problems and offers resonate.
audience: Agree the geography, company size, buyer roles, and exclusions together before building the first list.
scope_note: Sample scope for testing. Final audience, budget, and timeline need review before kickoff.
scope_intro: We handle research and campaign execution. Your team supplies the offer, approvals, and timely sales follow-up.
work1: Confirm the ideal customer, buyer roles, exclusions, and a small sample before scaling research.
work2: Research suitable prospects, check current roles and email validity, and remove duplicates and exclusions.
work3: Write focused messages and follow-ups. Check existing domains and inboxes before deciding what else is needed.
work4: Launch after approval, review human replies, and refine the audience and message as evidence comes in.
client1: Share customer examples, approved claims, account access, and do-not-contact lists.
client2: Review the target sample and copy. Name one person who can approve changes.
client3: Own buyer follow-up, discovery calls, quotations, and fulfilment.
launch_gate: We agree the audience, offer, copy, sending readiness, and reply owner before launch. No campaign starts without approval.
exclusions: Website work, full CRM rebuilds, paid ads, and sales closing are outside this pilot unless separately agreed.
timeline_intro: The pilot runs for 45 days from kickoff, with launch dependent on list quality, approvals, and sending readiness.
phase1: Review the setup, agree the audience, check a sample list, and approve the first messages.
phase2: Launch at a safe pace, review human replies, and check whether the right buyers are responding.
phase3: Refine the offer and targeting, document the results, and agree what should happen next.
timing_note: If access, approvals, or inbox readiness cause delays, agree a revised schedule before sending.
metric1: Company fit, role fit, current employment, exclusions, and email verification are separate checks.
metric2: Unique human respondents divided by unique people reached. Exclude automatic replies.
metric3: Interested respondents divided by human respondents, with counts and examples alongside the percentage.
metric4: Track qualified conversations and next steps. Revenue can follow after the pilot ends.
success: Use list quality, relevant replies, and sales conversations to judge the test. No reply rate, meeting count, or revenue outcome is guaranteed.
commercial_intro: This is a proposal for review. Confirm the scope and assumptions together before committing.
included: Research, email checks, copy, campaign setup, management, and reporting for the agreed scope.
tools: Tool costs are to be confirmed before kickoff. Existing client-owned sending accounts stay with the client.
ownership: The checked lead list, approved copy, campaign results, and access to your own sending accounts.
outside: Sales closing and fulfilment remain with your team. Additional work or tools need approval before purchase.
commercial_note: Missing commercial details are sample assumptions, not evidence of client approval. Confirm billing, tool costs, and any cancellation terms before kickoff.
next1: Review the proposal and resolve any open scope or budget questions.
next2: Confirm the agreement and payment, then share access and exclusions.
next3: Approve the sample audience and messages before launch.
final_note: A pilot is a test, not a performance guarantee. Nothing renews automatically.
